name: Teradata SPL
title: Teradata SPL (Database Engine 20)

presenceList.meta: Ec3, Ec4, D1, G1, G4, Q3

type.text: **NULL is a member of every domain**: procedure parameters, locals, and warehouse columns carry NULL unannounced, and no signature states whether a value may be absent
**No sum types**: an alternative is a nullable column, a status value, or a separate procedure, and the caller learns the encoding by reading the body
**Statements state no effect**: a procedure that loads tables, calls macros, and logs looks like any other in the DBC catalog
**C and Java ride the boundary**: external stored procedures bind compiled code through declared signatures, and the agreement on layout and error convention is checked by neither side's compiler

construction.text: **The procedure is one block**: CREATE PROCEDURE gathers DECLARE, flow, and SQL into one unit the database compiles into the catalog
**Macros sit beside procedures**: an EXEC macro is a parameterized SQL batch with no flow at all, and the boundary between the two unit kinds is a design decision the language does not guide

memory.text: **Allocation is the engine's**: spool, AMP memory, and cursor state live in the database processes, and the procedure text allocates nothing

error.text: **The handler decides, or the request aborts**: DECLARE ... HANDLER routes conditions and SQLSTATE codes, RESIGNAL re-raises, and without a handler the failure ends the request — no value carries it
**No composable result type**: failures travel by exception, results by OUT parameters and DYNAMIC RESULT SETS cursors, and neither composes through an expression

concurrency.text: **Session state is shared**: volatile tables and session-scoped cursor results are visible across every procedure the session calls, and the engine's workload management arbitrates the rest

platform.text: **The procedure runs only in Teradata**: the parser, the DBC dictionary, and the AMP architecture are the engine's, and nothing in the language runs without a Vantage system
**A poor fit outside warehouse work**: the language has no libraries or data abstraction beyond tables, so application logic builds every abstraction itself inside the warehouse

performance.text: **EXPLAIN is the ordinary tool**: the engine publishes the plan of any request, procedure statements included, and the docs treat it as the baseline cost instrument

ecosystem.text: **A niche commercial ecosystem**: expertise and tooling concentrate in enterprise warehouse shops, and the license terms govern every deployment
**A proprietary stack**: the engine, the tooling, and the support model are Teradata commercial products

evolution.text: **The engine line turned over**: Database Engine 20 replaces the 17.20 line (end of life announced for 2027), and deployments plan around the parity-and-upgrade path the release notes describe

domain.text: **The language exists to serve the warehouse**: procedures, macros, and external routines deploy into the DBC catalog, and the workload management and storage model define what they can say

learning.text: **Warehouse concepts before syntax**: AMP distribution, spool, and workload management decide whether a procedure performs, and the SPL book assumes that layer

syntax.text: **Standard-shaped, Teradata-flavored**: statements read like ISO SQL, and DYNAMIC RESULT SETS, volatile tables, and macro calls are the engine's own layer on top

testing.text: **No standard test harness for user procedures**: the documented testing story is application-side tests against a live system, with EXPLAIN as the only published instrument

security.text: **Dynamic SQL is string-built**: EXECUTE IMMEDIATE and PREPARE run text assembled at run time, so concatenated user input reaches the parser, and the mitigation is the privilege model plus USING inputs

reproducibility.text: **A procedure is stored source**: the same body on the same engine version and data reproduces the same result, and nothing is compiled ahead of the call
**No toolchain pin exists**: the repository names no engine version — the executing release is a deployment fact the system records elsewhere

supplychain.text: **No signed provenance for published procedures or external packages**: code moves through Teradata's commercial channels, with no signature-checked public distribution
**No public advisory feed for the engine's dependencies**: fixes land in Teradata release notes and support channels, with no CVE-mapped public advisory database

observability.text: **No tracing standard is part of the language**: DBQL logging, Viewpoint, and EXPLAIN are platform features, and the procedure text carries no trace hook
**No structured logging in the language**: SIGNAL text and the database's own logs are the output surface, and no logging construct exists in SPL

feedback.text: **No maintained editor analysis ships with the engine**: Teradata Studio's editors are basic, and code assistance lives in third-party SQL tools
**No procedure debugger ships with the engine**: diagnosis goes through EXPLAIN, DBQL, handler instrumentation, and the error log

interop.text: **No portable target**: the body compiles in one vendor's engine, and nothing in the language runs without a Teradata system

governance.text: **Governance is Teradata Corporation**: the release calendar, the EOL schedule, and the language's direction are one company's, and no independent body can change them
**No public specification exists**: the SQL Stored Procedures book documents the implemented behavior of one product line, and no independent implementation follows from it
**Correctness is what the engine does**: no conformance suite exists for SPL, and the one implementation is the oracle

tradeoffs: **Logic inside the warehouse**: procedures remove client round trips and run under the engine's workload management, and the price is application logic whose deploy, version, and license story is the platform's
**Result sets by cursor contract**: DYNAMIC RESULT SETS returns cursors to callers through the standard CLI, and the price is that the result shape is a cursor convention, not a type
**Macros and procedures share the stage**: the same logic can live as a flowless macro or a procedural block, and the price is a design decision the language documents but does not settle
**The engine line is a ratchet**: 17.20's announced end of life funnels deployments to Engine 20's parity path, and the price is an upgrade calendar set by the vendor
verdict: Teradata's SPL is the warehouse stored-procedure language of a proprietary platform: CREATE PROCEDURE over DECLARE, cursors with DYNAMIC RESULT SETS, condition handlers with SIGNAL and RESIGNAL, LOOP/WHILE/FOR flow, EXECUTE IMMEDIATE for dynamic SQL, and external procedures binding compiled C and Java. Its costs are the platform's own: NULL in every domain, failures that travel only by exception, session-wide volatile state, a niche commercial ecosystem, and single-vendor governance with no specification or conformance suite. Main strengths: EXPLAIN as an ordinary published tool, stored source the catalog compiles, and a release line (Engine 20, mid-2025) with a stated parity path off 17.20. Main weaknesses: no debugger or user-procedure test harness, no structured logging or tracing in the language, string-built dynamic SQL, basic editor tooling, and logic whose lifecycle — including the announced 2027 end of the previous line — rides one vendor's calendar.

energy.text: Energy is the AMPs': spool, distribution, and the warehouse's license bill pay, and the reader's levers are distribution and statement design the procedure exposes but does not control.

ai-readiness.text: Generated procedures appear in warehouse migration work, and the traps are the procedural layer: handler scope, result-set cursors, volatile state, and dynamic SQL no generated snippet prices.

safety.text: No certified path; the engine's transaction, fallback, and recovery guarantees are Teradata's, stated in its own documentation and support terms.

use:data.observation: procedures, macros, and external routines deploy into the DBC catalog

use:query.observation: results by OUT parameters and DYNAMIC RESULT SETS cursors

delivery.note: the database stores the source text, compiles it into the catalog, and executes it in place; no compiled unit crosses a producer boundary
